subject: history
title: An Indus city: upper town and lower town

nodes: Upper town (citadel): on a massive platform of baked brick
Lower town: houses of the common people
props.label: Mohenjodaro, p.28

scenes.narration: Mohenjodaro was a planned city with streets in a grid pattern: all the streets cut each other at right angles. The city was divided into two parts, the upper town and the lower town.

nodes: Upper town (citadel): on a massive platform of baked brick
Lower town: houses of the common people
props.label: p.28

scenes.narration: The upper town was built on a massive platform of baked brick. Archaeologists call it the citadel or acropolis. It might have been the administrative centre.

nodes: A well in the room beside the tank
Water fills the tank (waterproof with bitumen)
Steps from opposite sides to the bottom
Dirty water out to a brick drain
props.label: The Great Bath, p.29

scenes.narration: Within the citadel was the Great Bath: a rectangular tank of fired bricks, made waterproof with bitumen. A large well supplied water, steps led to the bottom, and used water drained out to a brick drain.

nodes: Covered drains along the main roads, cleaned regularly
props.label: Drainage, p.29

scenes.narration: The drains in houses led to a cesspool or manhole. The drains along the main roads were covered, and were inspected and cleaned regularly. This drainage system was remarkable among the cities of the world at that time.
